title: An objection stands until withdrawn
statement: In a review panel, an evidence-backed objection stands until whoever raised it withdraws it after a traced repair, and no vote settles a question of fact.
detail: A design for an adversarial review panel of AI agents treats silence as missing work, never assent, and lets a valid evidence-backed block stand until whoever raised it withdraws it after a traced repair. Its charter lets the panel adopt rules and plans but not vote facts into existence or grant approvals, which stay with named authorities. An audit of the build found remand passing generic error strings instead of the original blocking ballot and its evidence, and replacement ballots evaluated without the blocker withdrawing. The audit's scope notes conclude that a ten-agent vote cannot turn missing runtime evidence or missing human approval into fact.
against: The panel never ran and was retired: '- Live model work: **never started**.' (`grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/council-human-handover-2026-08-13/01_SCOPE_AND_TIMELINE.md`, line 66). A rule elsewhere accepts that an objection may be overruled and asks only that it be logged with its reasoning and rechecked in the next round.

evidence.quote: 9. Silence is missing work, never assent. A valid evidence-backed block survives until its author withdraws it after a traced repair.

The council may adopt a rule, implementation plan, critique disposition, or bounded course-design decision. It may not vote facts into existence or grant academic approval, source rights, item certification, live runtime proof, deployment, regulatory compliance, or student outcomes. Those remain with their named authorities.

Remand passed generic error strings rather than the original blocking ballot, author, evidence, challenged clauses, and ballot digest. Replacement ballots were evaluated without requiring the blocker to explicitly withdraw after a traced repair.
- A ten-agent vote cannot convert missing runtime evidence or missing human approval into fact.
